To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the orbifold fundamental groups for the moduli spaces of cubic surfaces and nonhyperelliptics of genus 3 are the factor groups of affine Artin groups defined in this thesis and that these groups can be used to give a presentation of the mapping classes of a compact genus 3 surface with connected boundary that can be understood from an algebro- geometric point of view.

the Artin groups are the right algebraic framework for the study of the orbifold fundamental groups and mapping class groups of moduli space of algebraic curves, and that the Artin group of a Coxeter graph can be defined as the quotient of the corresponding Artin group by a normal subgroup generated by certain elements.
the fundamental groups of modulis spaces of smooth curves are quotients of the mapping class of the underlying surfaces and that the mapping class groups are quotients of Artin groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between the theory of Artin groups, the theory of moduli spaces of curves, and the mapping class groups of compact surfaces.
the interplay between algebraic geometry, group theory and low-dimensional topology.
the study of the orbifold fundamental groups (or Artin groups) of certain moduli spaces of algebraic curves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mapping class group is the fundamental group of the moduli space, and the Artin group is the universal cover of the moduli stack.
the Artin groups are the natural algebraic objects to study the moduli spaces of algebraic curves.
we can use the geometry of the moduli space to get a presentation of the mapping classes of a genus three topological compact surface with a boundary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a new approach to the study of the moduli spaces of algebraic curves and their mapping class groups.
we show the existence of an algebro- geometrically meaningful presentation for the mapping class group in genus 3.
we give a geometric interpretation of the affine Coxeter graph of type $D_4$.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Artin groups of affine type play a role in algebraic geometry analogous to the role of Artin groups of spherical type in the theory of hyperbolic surfaces.
the fundamental groups of certain moduli spaces can be computed by means of a simple presentation of their orbifold fundamental groups.
Artin groups and their factor groups are useful tools for studying the fundamental groups of modulispaces of algebraic curves.
